methods.label: Compare root sums and products
methods.explanation:
Because the roots of each quadratic appear as coefficients of the other, compare their root sums and products. Expanding the first polynomial's linear factors gives
\[
(x-c)(x-d)=x^2-(c+d)x+cd.
\]
Matching coefficients with \(x^2+ax+b\), and doing the same for the other quadratic, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
c+d&=-a,& cd&=b,\\
a+b&=-c,& ab&=d.
\end{aligned}
\]
The sum relations say \(a+c=-d\) and \(a+c=-b\), so \(b=d\). Since \(b=d\ne0\), the product relations become \(ab=b\) and \(cb=b\). Dividing by the nonzero number \(b\) gives \(a=c=1\).

Now \(a+b=-c\) gives \(1+b=-1\), so \(b=d=-2\). These values satisfy the original conditions: both quadratics become
\[
x^2+x-2=(x-1)(x+2)=0,
\]
with roots \(1\) and \(-2\). Therefore
\[
a+b+c+d=1-2+1-2=\boxed{-2},
\]
choice B.
